text:
incident-bot: Paging: multiple GPU driver resets observed on infer-prod-2 (Xid 13/31 signatures). severity: P1. Creating INC-2026-110.

alex: seeing huge spike in driver resets starting ~11:07 UTC. telemetry shows container OOMs immediately after Xid in several pods.

mari: which node? I can grab kernel logs and nv-host logs.

alex: nodes affected: infer-prod-2-a03, infer-prod-2-a07, infer-prod-2-a09. 3/24 GPUs each.

eng-runtime-bot: Autoscaler: bridging to dedicated fallback pool for models rtx-medium and rtx-small. routing policy: prefer ded-prod-fallback.

dave: can we confirm Xid codes? nvml shows repeated Xid 13 then 31. Those map to ECC or illegal memory access.

alex: grabbing dmesg now, dropping excerpt:

```
[Nov 12 11:09:14] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=23745, GPU=0
[Nov 12 11:09:14] nvidia: GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[Nov 12 11:09:15] kernel: oom-killer: Killed process 23745 (runtime-server) total-vm: 1254324kB
```

mari: that's consistent with a driver-level reset then immediate oom in the runtime container. could be leaking host memory or corrupted dma mappings.

karen: customer impact: alerting shows ~4% 500s on hosted API, mostly generation endpoints for medium models. SLAs degraded for a subset of requests.

alex: routing team, can we temporarily shift traffic off infer-prod-2 region until we stabilize?

eng-runtime-bot: Route manager: applied canary-route to move 60% of new sessions to us-east-1-dedicated for affected model families. Existing sessions remain pinned.

mari: I'm going to cordon and drain the most noisy node (a07) to prevent cascade. will evict pods and let autoscaler spin replacements in healthy AZ.

alex: patch to kube drain command I'm running:

```
kubectl cordon infer-prod-2-a07
kubectl drain infer-prod-2-a07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

karen: heads-up to support: customers A and C see elevated errors; will open status page blurb. minimal customer-facing text: "We’re investigating increased errors for generation API; working on mitigation."

eng-runtime-bot: Diagnostic bundle collected for infer-prod-2-a07 -> /artifacts/INC-2026-110/diagnostics/a07.tar.gz

mari: attaching quick kernel oops excerpt:

```
[11:08:59] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU memory corruption detected (ECC corrected errors: 12)
[11:09:01] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

alex: ECC corrected errors are creeping up. Suggest we set node to maintenance and run memtest-like workload / vendor diagnostics. Might be failing GPU hardware.

dave: agree. plan: cordon a03 and a09 next, run vendor diagnostic tool on a07 first. If hardware failing, we'll swap to spare nodes and mark the GPUs unhealthy in inventory.

mari: started vendor diag (nvidia-smi diag) on a07, ETA ~10m. also dumping container logs for runtime-server to check for memory alloc patterns.

karen: support: posting status page update now. linking to internal incident: INC-2026-110.

support-bot: Status page updated: "Investigating increased 500 responses for Generation API, partial degradation for some customers."

alex: quick mitigation we applied: 1) route 60% new sessions to dedicated fallback, 2) cordon+drain a07, 3) autoscaler provisioning replacements. still seeing a small tail of errors from existing sessions.

mari: diag finished: vendor tool reports transient ECC errors and recommends GPU reseat and further tests. no permanent failure yet but high corrected ECC counts.

dave: reseat takes ~15m per host with infra team. Recommend evaporating workload off nodes and scheduling maintenance tonight for full reseat+stress. For now, mark GPUs as degraded to avoid scheduling heavy jobs.

alex: setting runtime scheduler bump to avoid large-batch jobs on degraded nodes. command: 

```
redwoodctl runtime update-scheduling --node infer-prod-2-a03 --degraded true
```

eng-runtime-bot: Scheduler update accepted for nodes a03,a09. New tasks will avoid GPUs flagged degraded.

karen: customer-impact note: affected customers: cust-alpha (10% request failure), cust-beta (time-limited rate reductions). Ops will contact enterprise accounts in parallel.

mari: we should capture a trace for a killed container to ensure it's not a runtime allocation bug. alex, can you attach heap/profile from the runtime-server core?

alex: got core dump; uploading to /artifacts/INC-2026-110/coredumps/runtime-server-a07.gz. sending to eng-ml for inspection.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary fallback successful: 60% traffic routed, error rate on fallback nodes down to baseline. Overall platform error rate reduced from 4% to 1.2%.

dave: next steps: 1) keep nodes cordoned and drained, 2) run hardware reseat+extended vendor stress tonight, 3) if ECC counters continue to climb after reseat, escalate RMA.

mari: proceeding with reseat schedule: infra ops will do a07 at 23:00 UTC, a03 and a09 tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

karen: support is drafting customer emails and has prioritized enterprise outreach.

alex: handing to oncall-north for overnight: please watch for reappearance of Xid 13/31 and customer alerts. I've left diagnostics pointers in INC ticket.

oncall-north: acknowledged. will monitor and escalate if resets reappear. Contact: dave oncall 2 for urgent hardware swap.

incident-bot: INC-2026-110 updated: mitigation in place (traffic reroute, nodes cordoned), progress: >70% of affected pods moved to fallback.

karen: tagging postmortem: owners alex + dave + mari. we'll schedule RCA tomorrow.

alex: logging final notes: probable root cause = elevated ECC corrected errors leading to driver resets -> container OOMs. mitigations = traffic routing, cordon/drain, vendor diagnostics and reseat. handing off to overnight oncall.

oncall-north: handoff accepted. good job team. :thumbsup:
